classes.SIG-ONLY-NULL: a no-difference label issued because a CI contains 0 (or a significance gate failed); no equivalence band
classes.POINT-IN-BAND: a no-difference label issued because a POINT estimate lies inside a band; the band exists but the CI is ignored
classes.POINT-ONLY-LINE: a one-sided 'not material' label issued because a POINT estimate is below a materiality line; the CI is ignored
classes.CI-OVERLAP-SAME: a 'same' label issued because one book's point estimate lies inside the other's CI; no band, not a test of the difference
classes.LOSS-WITHOUT-SIGN: a 'loss' label that does not require the realised mean of the book(s) named to be negative (K1 family)
classes.BAND-NOT-GATING: an equivalence band exists and is computed, but the label it should gate is issued without it
classes.PRECEDENCE: the no-difference branch is evaluated before the direction branches, so it can override a significant (A)/(B)
classes.ABSENT-AS-NULL: a missing statistic (None / no rows) falls through to the 'not material' branch
classes.FAILED-GATE-AS-ABSENCE: a failed detection/admission gate is written up as absence of the effect, without an upper bound below a usefulness line
classes.PROSE-EQUIVALENCE: the device label is honest (UNDECIDED), but a decision document restates it as 'indistinguishable'
classes.COMPLIANT: the label is CI-based against an explicit band or economic line in the direction of the claim
classes.OUT-OF-SCOPE: deterministic tolerance, percentile position, set overlap, admission or descriptive output: not a sampling-based no-difference claim
